analysis:
This PR adds a TTFT 'shape warmup' to the provider: synthetic, excluded calibration cells run after model load. The changes are in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (new Cell.sampled, ShapeWarmupMode via the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env var, shader-cache probe, shapeWarmup cell generator, new state fields), ProviderLoop+ModelCalibration.swift:17-24 (fallback to startShapeWarmupIfNeeded when calibration does not start), ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:237 and 343-350 (shapeWarmup dependency run before registration), and StandaloneServer+StartupPreload.swift (a startup hook and a sweep-tick retry).

Security-relevant observations:
- The warmup prompts are synthetic, with no consumer data. Cell sizing is derived from local constants and engine parameters, so I found no new plaintext exposure (A-001) and no key handling change (A-003).
- The environment variable only toggles a performance feature. It is read from the process environment, which is operator-controlled and already within the operator trust boundary (TB-003).
- Availability: the warmup is bounded by shapeWarmupBudgetSeconds=20 and a 500 ms grace, and is documented as preemptible by any request. The startup path is bounded by the registration gate timeout. This is consistent with T-029 and T-010. I did not see the implementations of runShapeWarmupBeforeServing, startShapeWarmupIfNeeded and startModelCalibrationIfNeeded, so I could not verify the preemption and budget enforcement, or that the changed Bool return of startModelCalibrationIfNeeded matches its callers.
- Prefix cache (T-041): sampled warmup prompts of roughly 4.3k+ tokens could be donated to the SSD prefix cache if the warmup does not bypass donation. Synthetic content would then add a wear/disk footprint. I could not verify that the warmup bypasses donation or uses an excluded measurement purpose, as the startup self-test does with .startupWarmup. The engine-side implementation is outside the supplied evidence.
- The ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift base and head text were reviewed. The patch-only files were reviewed via patch hunks only.

Open question for the next pass: confirm that the EngineV2Bridge shape warmup (a) bypasses the prefix-cache donation and TTFT-oracle surfaces, (b) does not count toward routing or perf telemetry, (c) cannot run while real traffic is in flight or hold the KV grant against real requests, and (d) is gated on the same idle/drain conditions as calibration.
